correctness.rationale: Reducing modulo the radical forces all vertex-idempotent coefficients of a root to vanish (a field has no nonzero square-zero scalar). In J^3=0 the degree-two part of the root is then free and contributes q^n, leaving the cyclic products u_i u_(i+1). For Y=0, a support is independent on the cycle; conditioning on a chosen vertex gives the two weighted path terms. For a mixed target, the nonzero edges force their incident vertices and form disjoint paths, each with one multiplicative degree of freedom. At a zero gap of length L there are L−1 internal vertices. The two outermost internal vertices are forced zero (the same vertex for L=2); L=1 is impossible and the remaining max(0,L−3) vertices support an independent set. This proves the fiber for all nonzero edge labels, including characteristic two. Full support leaves one cyclic consistency equation: even length requires equal alternating products and leaves q−1 starters; odd length identifies the square of the starter and gives the stated image correction. Legal mixed binary words are exactly those avoiding the cyclic triple 101; the closed walks of the displayed pair-state matrix weight each labelled pattern once and cannot admit 101. Its characteristic polynomial is t(t^3−qt^2+(q−1)t−(q−1)); the positive-weight pair graph is irreducible and aperiodic. With w=q−1, the cubic signs are negative at w and positive at w+1, and its derivative is nonnegative at w and strictly increasing on [w,infinity), identifying the Perron root in that interval. The other eigenvalues and the O(w^n) torus correction are lower order at fixed q. The frozen checker counts arrow-coordinate solutions, not the free factor q^n; the argument supplies that factor exactly.
residual_risks: Scope is targets in J² and truncation length three; the entropy limit fixes q. No formal proof-assistant claim.
